findings.claim: Reclassifying an oversized manifest from SnapshotError::Corrupt to SnapshotError::Limit changes the variant observed by every existing caller of GraphSnapshotManifest::validate() (reader open, activation, GC paths across compass-store-redb/compass-graphdb/compass-cli), and the packet contains no call-site audit showing none of them branch on the Corrupt variant (e.g., for fallback, quarantine, or error-mapping behavior).
findings.evidence: Hunk in `GraphSnapshotManifest::validate` replacing the combined `graph_bytes == 0 || graph_bytes > MAX_GRAPH_BYTES` Corrupt arm with `SnapshotError::canonical_graph_too_large(...)` (a `Limit` variant) for the oversized case; the diff shows no grep or test evidence that `match` sites on `SnapshotError::Corrupt` were reviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Audit all consumers of SnapshotError (rg 'SnapshotError::Corrupt' and 'SnapshotError::Limit' across crates/) and either confirm variant-agnostic handling or update any Corrupt-specific branching to also handle Limit; note the result in the design doc.

findings.claim: digest_json is generic over any serializable payload (`fn digest_json<T: Serialize>(value: &T, maximum: usize)`), but the failure it now returns unconditionally advises graph-scope remediation (`--exclude <pattern>`, `.compassignore`), so any current or future non-graph call site (e.g., selector or delta digest encoding in the same module) would emit a misleading recovery action tied to an unrelated limit.
findings.evidence: Hunk in `digest_json` replacing the plain limit message with `SnapshotError::canonical_graph_too_large(maximum as u64)`; the constructor hardcodes 'canonical graph exceeds ... retry or rebuild with a smaller scope using --exclude <pattern> or persistent patterns in .compassignore' regardless of what `value` was being encoded.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make digest_json graph-specific (rename to digest_canonical_graph_json) or have it return a neutral Limit and attach the scope-remediation suffix only at the canonical-graph publication call site.

findings.claim: The CLI regression passes the graph path to the binary via `graph_path.to_string_lossy()`, which silently mangles non-UTF-8 paths; on Windows temp directories with non-UTF-8 components the test would exercise a path that is not the real artifact path, weakening the platform-portable guarantee the constraint requires.
findings.evidence: `.args(["search", "sample", "--graph", graph_path.to_string_lossy().as_ref(), ...])`; constraint `platform-portable`: 'No assumption of UTF-8 paths ... without a guarded implementation and test.'
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the path as an OsStr argument (`graph_path.as_os_str()`) so the test exercises the exact artifact path on all platforms.
